cards.text: It's the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, and the LORD speaks to His prophet Jeremiah. Take a scroll, He says, and write on it all the words I've spoken to you about Israel, Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you under Josiah until today. Friend, that's not a sticky note. That's a WHOLE career.

cards.question: God wants the people of Judah to hear about the calamity He plans to bring on them. What does He hope each of them will do?

answers.text: Turn from his wicked way
Run to Egypt for safety
Rebuild the walls of Jerusalem

cards.question: Jeremiah has years of the LORD's words to get onto that scroll. Who does he call to write them down as he speaks?

answers.text: Baruch son of Neriah
Elisha son of Shaphat
Joshua son of Nun

cards.text: Baruch writes down every word as Jeremiah dictates, and then there's a snag: Jeremiah says he's restricted and can't enter the house of the LORD. Biggest project of your life, finally DONE, and your badge won't open the door.

cards.question: Jeremiah can't go into the house of the LORD himself. What does he tell Baruch to do there?

answers.text: Read the scroll aloud to the people
Hide the scroll in the treasury
Hand the scroll to the priests

cards.question: Jeremiah tells Baruch to go read the scroll at the house of the LORD on a day of ___.

answers.text: fasting
harvest
celebration

cards.question: Jeremiah hopes the people will bring their petition before the LORD and turn from their wicked ways. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD's anger against them is great
The king himself asked for a warning
The armies of Babylon are at the gate

cards.text: Baruch does everything Jeremiah commanded him. Then, in the ninth month of Jehoiakim's fifth year, a fast before the LORD is called, and people come to Jerusalem from the cities of Judah, so the house is PACKED.
Baruch reads from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, up in the upper courtyard by the New Gate. Every person there hears it.

cards.question: Gemariah's son Micaiah hears all the words of the LORD from the scroll. Where does he go next?

answers.text: The scribe's chamber in the king's palace
The prophet Jeremiah's house
The gate of the city wall

cards.text: All the officials are sitting there, including Elishama the scribe and Micaiah's own father, Gemariah. Micaiah tells them everything Baruch read, and I bet you could hear a sprinkle drop in that room.

cards.question: The officials send a man named Jehudi to Baruch with a message. What is it?

answers.text: Bring the scroll and come here
Take the scroll to the priests
Stop reading the scroll in public

cards.text: When Baruch arrives, the officials say, "Please sit down," and ask him to read it to them. So he does, and two readings in, this man is officially ON TOUR.

cards.question: The officials hear every word Baruch reads from the scroll. How do they react?

answers.text: They turn to one another in fear
They laugh and wave it all off
They walk out before Baruch finishes

cards.question: After hearing the scroll, the officials tell Baruch they must report all these words to the king.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: The officials ask Baruch how he wrote all these words. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Jeremiah recited them and he wrote them in ink
He copied them from an older scroll
He heard them in a dream one night

cards.question: The officials are about to take these words to the king. What do they tell Baruch and Jeremiah to do?

answers.text: Hide and tell no one where they are
Flee from Judah down to Egypt
Come and stand before the king

cards.text: Hide, and tell no one where you are. Friend, when the king's OWN officials tell you to hide from the king, you don't ask follow-up questions. You HIDE.

The officials store the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, then go to King Jehoiakim in the courtyard and report everything. I would pay a whole box of cookies to see the faces in that meeting.

cards.question: King Jehoiakim hears the officials' report about the scroll. What does he do next?

answers.text: Sends Jehudi to get the scroll
Sends for Jeremiah to explain it
Calls for the priests to pray

cards.text: It's the ninth month, so the king is in his winter quarters with a fire burning in front of him, while Jehudi reads to him and his officials. Warm fire, comfy seat, a nice reading, what could POSSIBLY go wrong?

cards.question: Jehudi reads the scroll to King Jehoiakim by the fire. Every time Jehudi gets through three or four columns, what does the king do?

answers.text: Cuts them off and throws them in the fire
Hands them to an official to keep
Tells Jehudi to read them once more

cards.question: Jehoiakim cuts the columns with a scribe's ___ and keeps going until the entire scroll is ___ by the fire.

answers.text: knife
consumed
pen
saved
sealed

cards.text: Snip, into the fire, snip, into the fire, until the whole scroll is gone. I spent years in a drawer full of takeout menus NOBODY ever read, and not even THEY got thrown in a fire.

cards.question: As King Jehoiakim and his servants hear all these words, they become frightened and tear their garments.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: While the scroll burns, three officials named Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah speak up. What do they do?

answers.text: Urge the king not to burn it
Help throw columns into the fire
Leave the room without a word

cards.question: Jehoiakim won't listen to those three officials. Instead, he gives an order about Baruch and Jeremiah. What is it?

answers.text: Seize Baruch and Jeremiah
Banish them from Jerusalem
Bring them to read it again

cards.question: The king sends three men to seize Baruch and Jeremiah. But who had hidden them?

answers.text: The LORD
Jehudi
The Rechabites

cards.text: After the king burns the scroll, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah. Jehoiakim had the fire. God still has the last word.

cards.question: The first scroll is burned up. What does the LORD tell Jeremiah to do now?

answers.text: Write the very same words on another scroll
Stop speaking to the king for good
Leave Jerusalem with Baruch at once

cards.text: The LORD also has a message for Jehoiakim, and He quotes the king's own question back to him: why did you write that the king of Babylon would surely come and destroy this land? When your own words get read back to you, friend, the meeting is NOT going your way.

cards.question: Because Jehoiakim burned the scroll, the LORD says he will have no one to sit on ___ throne.

answers.text: David's
Pharaoh's
Nebuchadnezzar's

cards.question: The LORD says Jehoiakim's body will be buried with honor beside his fathers.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: The LORD says He will bring all the calamity He warned about on Jehoiakim, Jerusalem and the men of Judah. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They did not listen to His warning
They broke a treaty with Egypt
They traded with distant nations

cards.question: Jeremiah gives Baruch another scroll, and as Jeremiah dictates, Baruch writes all the words of the burned scroll again. Many similar words are added to them.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: The king burned the message, and he got it back with MORE words on it. That's like deleting an email you don't like and waking up to the EXTENDED version.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'It's the fourth year…', 'Take a scroll, He says…', 'Friend, that's not a sticky note.' and 'That's a WHOLE career.' The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: 'so the house is PACKED' states a crowd as fact. Jeremiah 36:9 only says a fast was proclaimed to the people of Jerusalem and to those who came from Judah's cities. It does not mention the house of the LORD or how full it was. The exaggeration is told as narration, not as Papa Dorin's own joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card cites Jeremiah 36:11-12, but the right answer (the scribe's chamber in the king's palace) comes only from 36:12. Verse 11 is part of the question setup.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The card cites Jeremiah 36:17-18, but the right answer (Jeremiah recited the words and Baruch wrote them in ink) comes from Baruch's reply in 36:18. Verse 17 is the officials' question, which is the setup.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: This story card repeats Jeremiah 36:19 ('Hide, and tell no one where you are'), which card 17 just asked and answered. It adds a joke but does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This story card retells Jeremiah 36:23 ('Snip, into the fire… until the whole scroll is gone'), which cards 4 and 5 already asked and answered. It is a recap with a joke on it and does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 36:31 gives the reason as 'for their iniquity.' 'but they did not listen' describes the calamity they were warned about. Presenting 'They did not listen to His warning' as 'the reason He gives' changes what the text calls the reason. Also, the question's wording ('the calamity He warned about') echoes the right answer ('His warning'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card restates Jeremiah 36:32 (the burned message rewritten with more words added), which card 17 just asked and answered. It is a recap with a joke on it and does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
